official_measurement_examples.name: Strategic map modelling limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Defra explains that 2022 strategic noise maps were produced by modelling rather than site measurements and do not necessarily represent the exact current sound level at a locality on a particular day.

official_measurement_examples.name: Five-year mapping cycle
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environmental-noise regulations require periodic strategic mapping and action planning; the maps are primarily tools for identifying exposure patterns and priority areas.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning thresholds limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning practice guidance warns that numerical noise criteria in supporting documents should not be treated as fixed universal thresholds that determine every planning outcome.

official_measurement_examples.name: Round 4 data scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2022 Round 4 road and rail collections describe annual-average modelled indicators such as Lden, Lnight and daytime equivalent levels, not instantaneous readings.

official_measurement_examples.name: Legacy-round date preservation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Round 2 and Round 3 datasets republished in July 2026 still describe modelling undertaken for 2012 or 2017 and must retain those source years rather than being mislabelled as 2026 measurements.

official_measurement_examples.name: Permit noise separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency noise and vibration guidance updated May 2026 applies to environmental-permit assessments and does not substitute for planning permission or local statutory-nuisance decisions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Statutory nuisance legal test
official_measurement_examples.fact: Councils investigate potential statutory nuisance using context such as level, duration, frequency, timing and locality; a strategic map band alone is not a statutory-nuisance determination.

official_measurement_examples.name: Transport-noise statutory nuisance distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government nuisance guidance distinguishes statutory nuisance rules from traffic and aircraft noise regimes, so those controls must not be merged into a single parcel noise-clearance flag.

core_rules: strategic noise-map polygons are modelled annual-average evidence not site measurements
a 2026 dataset page update does not change a 2012 or 2017 modelling year
Lden and Lnight indicators must retain their defined time-weighting and averaging scope
noise planning guidance does not impose one universal numeric planning threshold
a strategic high-noise band is not automatic planning refusal
absence from a mapped band is not proof of acceptable site acoustics
environmental-permit noise assessment is distinct from planning permission
statutory-nuisance determination is distinct from strategic noise mapping
road rail aviation and industrial noise regimes must not be silently merged
noise-action-plan priority status is not parcel ownership or permission evidence
a noise management plan is not proof of final compliance
historic noise maps must retain round source year and modelling methodology
noise compliance does not reserve development capacity or access rights
site-specific receptors and proposal use remain necessary context
no parcel noise clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official GOV.UK, Defra, Environment Agency and National Data Library sources were checked on 2026-07-26. March-July 2026 catalogue updates and May 2026 permit guidance were retained without relabelling older model years as current site measurements.
